'''Sonia Isabelle Seneviratne''' (born on 5 June 1974 in [[Lausanne]]<ref>[http://www.iac.ethz.ch/people-iac/person-detail.html?persid=54778 ''Curriculum Vitae'']</ref>) is a Swiss climate scientist, professor at the Institute for Atmospheric and Climate Science of the [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name=ibtimes>{{Cite web|title = Investments in Renewable Energy Being Questioned Following Hiatus of Global Warming|url = http://www.ibtimes.com.au/investments-renewable-energy-being-questioned-following-hiatus-global-warming-1333548|work = [[International Business Times]]|access-date = 29 October 2015|date = 28 February 2014}}</ref> She is a specialist of [[extreme weather|extreme climate events]].

== Biography ==

Sonia Seneviratne studied [[biology]] at the [[University of Lausanne]] and [[environmental sciences]] at the [[ETH Zurich]]. In 2002, she received a PhD in atmospheric and climate science from [[ETH Zurich]].

She worked as [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[National Aeronautics and Space Administration]]. Since 2007, she is professor at the Institute for Atmospheric and Climate Science of the [[ETH Zurich]].

Sonia Seneviratne is a member of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] (IPCC). She was a lead author of the IPCC's [[Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5&nbsp;°C]] (2018)<ref>{{citation |series=Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5&nbsp;°C |quote="IPCC special report on the impacts of global warming of 1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels and related global [[greenhouse gas emissions|greenhouse gas emission]] pathways, in the context of strengthening the global response to the threat of climate change, sustainable development, and efforts to eradicate poverty |title=Summary for Policymakers|publisher=[[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] (IPCC) |date=n.d. |access-date=8 October 2018 |url=http://report.ipcc.ch/sr15/pdf/sr15_spm_final.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite report |title=Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C |publisher=[[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] (IPCC) |date=7 October 2018 |access-date=7 October 2018 |location=[[Incheon]], [[Republic of Korea]] |url=https://www.ipcc.ch/report/sr15/}}</ref> and a coordinating lead author of the [[IPCC Sixth Assessment Report|Sixth Assessment Report]] (2021).<ref>{{Cite web|title=IPCC Authors (beta)|url=https://apps.ipcc.ch/report/authors/report.authors.php?q=35&p=|access-date=2021-08-08|website=apps.ipcc.ch}}</ref>

In 2025, her team published in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' an analysis showing that the emissions of [[Big oil|oil giants]] made 213 [[heatwaves]] (reported over 2000–2023) more intense and 200 times more likely.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Quilcaille, Yann |author2=Gudmundsson, Lukas |author3=Schumacher, Dominik |author4=Gasser, Thomas |author5=Heede, Richard |author6=Heri, Corina |author7=Lejeune, Quentin |author8=Nath, Shruti |author9=Naveau, Philippe |author10=Thiery, Wim |author11=Schleussner, Carl-Friedrich |author12=Seneviratne, Sonia |title=Systematic attribution of heatwaves to the emissions of carbon majors |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume=645 |pages=392–398 |date=10 September 2025 |doi=10.1038/s41586-025-09450-9 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09450-9 |access-date=15 September 2025|hdl=20.500.11850/786600 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Damian Carrington |date=10 September 2025 |title=Carbon emissions from oil giants directly linked to dozens of deadly heatwaves for first time |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2025/sep/10/link-oil-giants-heatwaves-research-legal-liability |website=theguardian.com |publisher=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=15 September 2025}}</ref>

== Honours ==

Sonia Seneviratne was included in [[Thomson Reuters]]'s 2015 list of the most cited modern scientists.<ref>{{cite web|title=Highly Cited Researchers 2015|url=http://highlycited.com/#Seneviratne|publisher=[[Thomson Scientific]]}}</ref> She was the lead author on a 2014 article in Nature Climate Change that showed no pause in the increase of hot temperature extremes from 1997 to 2012.<ref name=ibtimes/><ref>{{Cite web|title = No global warming 'hiatus' for extreme heat days|url = http://www.cbc.ca/news/technology/no-global-warming-hiatus-for-extreme-heat-days-1.2551270|website = CBC News|access-date = 29 October 2015}}</ref>

She is a [[Roger Revelle Medal|Revelle Medal]] committee member.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sites.agu.org/leadership/committees/council-committees/medal-selection-committees/revelle-medal-committee/|title=Revelle Medal Committee – Leadership|website=agu.org}}</ref> In 2013, she received the [[James B. Macelwane Medal]] from the [[American Geophysical Union]].<ref name=AGU>{{cite web|title=SONIA I. SENEVIRATNE 2013 James B. Macelwane Medal Winner|url=http://honors.agu.org/winners/sonia-i-seneviratne/|publisher=[[American Geophysical Union]]}}</ref> In 2014, she received a consolidator grant from the [[European Research Council]].
